maria: Heads-up — CVE came in for the NVIDIA driver package we ship (privilege escalation vector in kernel module loader). vendor advisory says patched drivers are signed and blob layout changed. need triage on compatibility with our CUDA/cuDNN/NCCL matrix and questions on KMS signing for private builds. :warning:

devon: thanks. can we get a quick impact matrix? Which clusters/current driver versions exposed?

maria: affected: driver 525.x and earlier. our hosted pools mostly on 525.2, some dedicated on 530.x. quick list: hosted-eu (525.2), hosted-us (525.4), dedicated-gpu-large (530.1), private-customer-a (525.0).

aj: priority-wise: patching the hosted pools should be P0 for security, but we need an interoperability smoke before mass rollout. if signed driver blob changes, older CUDA runtime + signed driver could break kernel interfaces.

kai: @aj agree. suggest staged rollout: canary on a small pool with representative CUDA/cuDNN/NCCL combos. smoke tests: model-serving latency, mem leak, cuda init logs. add automated check: run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` and our test harness.

ops-jen: notes on RBAC/audit side — driver rollouts need elevated infra perms. planning a short-lived role for the rollout job (`driver-rollout-runner`) with scoped permissions and audit logging turned on. Audit logs must include which key (KMS) used to sign packages and who triggered the job.

maria: KMS question: we currently have package signing keys in HSM for private builds. vendor-signed drivers require our internal re-sign? or we host signed blobs from vendor? vendor recommends customers sign with their own KMS for proprietary modules. thoughts?

devon: two options: 1) accept vendor-signed binaries (faster) but need to validate trust chain and update whitelisting; 2) re-sign with our KMS — slower and requires build infra changes + RBAC for key access. For private deployments (air-gapped) re-signing is likely mandatory.

aj: security tradeoff: vendor-signed is ok for hosted but for Dedicated/Private we should re-sign with customer/KMS. Also need to ensure our SBOM and attestations record signing key IDs.

kai: compatibility validation plan: pick 3 representative CUDA versions (11.8, 12.1, 12.3), two cuDNN variants, and NCCL 2.x/3.x. Run the following in canary: unit/gpu-integration tests, pytorch/generic inference smoke, multi-GPU NCCL allreduce. If any fail, fallback to previous driver for that pool.

security-bot: CVE-2026-XXXX severity: HIGH. CVSS 7.8. public exploit: low. Recommended action: patch and verify.

ops-jen: rollout playbook draft: 1) create `driver-rollout-runner` role (scope: image-push, node-restart) 2) prepare signed build artifacts (vendor-signed for hosted canary) 3) canary on 2 nodes (mixed CUDA) 4) run compatibility harness (automated) 5) if green, incrementally roll 10% every 30m with health gates 6) write audit event to audit.s3 (KMS-encrypted) with key metadata and commit hash.

maria: immediate TODOs: - @kai assemble canary matrix and test harness snippets - @devon validate vendor trust chain and policy for accepting vendor-signed blobs - @ops-jen create RBAC role and add audit sink - I'll coordinate Dedicated/Private signing policy with legal/compliance folks.

aj: timeline: want canary by EOD tomorrow. if any step blocks, escalate to infra on-call.

kai: working on harness now, dropping initial script here:```
# canary test run
./run_gpu_smoke --driver /artifacts/nvidia-530.2.run --cuda 12.1 --test-suite smoke_basic,nccl_allreduce
```

maria: perfect. please post canary logs to #incidents if any failures. tagging @sre on-call for awareness. :eyes: 

security-bot: action created: sec-1234 (driver-triage) assigned to devon, due 2026-03-22.
